problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=-3{x}^{2}+1$ defined on $[-3,3).$  Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension of $G(x)=-6x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
-3{x}^{2}+1∼-8+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{108(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is

$$
-6x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-4}}\cdot {{field-5}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and we are already given the coefficients ${a}_{0}$ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼-8+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{108(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, notice that 

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-3,3),$

- continuous on $[-3,3),$ and

- satisfies $F(-3)=F(3),$ if we extend the value at $x=3$ using the formula $F(x)=-3{x}^{2}+1.$

Therefore, the $6$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{continuous}$ and $\text{piecewise smooth}$ on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3{x}^{2}+1) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-8)+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{108(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\ -6x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{108(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\ -6x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-36(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\ -6x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{36(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$
